subject: Buyer risk profile and contract tenor alignment for AWS private offer — AcmeData
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmedata.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Buyer risk profile and contract tenor alignment for AWS private offer — AcmeData

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, AcmeData’s procurement team flagged two things that will determine the final private-offer terms: buyer-side approval windows (who signs and how long approvals take) and the buyer risk profile (data residency/compliance constraints). I want to align internally and propose a couple of concrete paths so we can move the PO to signature quickly.

Quick summary of what we heard:
- Procurement prefers a single PO covering a 24-month commitment but is open to 12 months if there are stronger SLA/credits.
- They need clarity on where logs and audit data live (US-only) and a short cert pack for SOC 2 scope.
- Buyer approvals may require VP-level signoff at Acme — likely a 7–14 business-day window.

Options I recommend (we can tailor):
1) 24-month private offer with 8% annualized discount, standard Redwood SOC 2 + signed data processing addendum (US-only restriction). Requires procurement + legal review but shortens renewal friction.
2) 12-month private offer at 6% discount plus a 30-day SLA credit guarantee and a two-week expedited approval window (we provide a dedicated SOW and priority onboarding).

Attached is a draft PO and a redline-friendly doc with the two paths called out (acmedata_draft_po_20260820.pdf; redlines_acme_20260820.docx). Can you confirm which path procurement prefers and who the final signatory will be so we can set the private offer parameters in AWS Marketplace?

If helpful, Vanessa and Karthik are looped for internal approval lanes. Proposed next step: a 30-minute call Friday to lock the path so I can send the private-offer link and DocuSign.

Best,
Rafael
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

---
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmedata.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmedata.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Buyer risk profile and contract tenor alignment for AWS private offer — AcmeData

Rafael —

Appreciate the clear options. A few clarifications from procurement that will affect the decision:

1) Signatory: Finance VP (Maya Carter) will need to sign for spend above $250k.
2) Data residency: the service must guarantee that audit logs and telemetry are stored in us-east-1; we also need a short SOC 2 summary and contact for an attestation.
3) Approval window: Procurement will try to target 10 business days but it depends on legal redlines — if Redwood can limit redlines around indemnity/liability we can probably hit that.

On discount: Maya is inclined to favor predictable costs over an aggressive discount. A 24-month commit is possible if there is an automatic annual renewal clause and a termination-for-convenience cap tied to an SLA credit.

Next steps from our side: I’ll confirm with Maya whether she prefers 12 vs 24, but procurement asked if you can prepare:
- A marketplace private-offer that lists a 24-month term but allows a 1-month early-exit with a capped fee tied to remaining committed spend.
- A SOC 2 summary + Redwood security contact.

Can we get the private-offer draft and the SOC 2 summary by EOD tomorrow? If so, we’ll aim to lock signatures within 10 business days.

Thanks —
Alex Nguyen
Senior Procurement Manager
AcmeData

Subject: Re: Buyer risk profile and contract tenor alignment for AWS private offer — AcmeData

Alex —

We can do that. Quick answers and attachments coming:

- SOC 2: attaching a one-page SOC 2 summary and contact (sec-contacts@redwood.com). We will provide the full report under NDA if required.
- Private-offer structure: I will prepare a private-offer proposal with the 24-month term and an early-exit option (one-month notice + capped termination fee equal to 25% of remaining committed value).
- SLA credits: propose a 2% monthly credit for missed latency SLOs, and a cumulative cap we can discuss with legal.

I’ve attached the draft PO and redlines (same attachments as earlier). Vanessa/Karthik — can you confirm internal approval lanes on Redwood’s side? Specifically:
- Vanessa: do we need an exec signoff to approve a one-month early-exit clause?
- Karthik: will legal accept the proposed 25% cap or do you recommend a lower exposure for Redwood?

Alex — if you can confirm Maya’s signatory preference (name/title) today, I’ll aim to get the private-offer and SOC summary over by EOD tomorrow and include the DocuSign path to speed the signature.

Thanks,
Rafael

---

Date: 2026-08-21T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Buyer risk profile and contract tenor alignment for AWS private offer — AcmeData

Rafael / Karthik —

Quick internal note on approvals:
- Exec signoff: I can approve the one-month early-exit clause at the director level for this deal, provided legal signs off on the indemnity/LI clause. No CEO-level approval needed.
- Exposure cap: Karthik — suggest we start with 20% termination fee exposure and a hard cap on cumulative SLA credits at 6 months of fees. That keeps economics bounded while staying competitive.
- Timeline: once Rafael uploads the private-offer link and the SOC summary, I’ll greenlight an expedited legal review (3 business days) for the redline set you sent.

Action items:
- Rafael: send private-offer draft + SOC 2 summary (EOD tomorrow).
- Karthik: prepare a short legal note on indemnity/liability margin we can accept and confirm the 20% vs 25% recommendation.

I’ll standby to escalate to VP if procurement pushes additional terms.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Marketplace Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
